You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object.

KNOWN BUG: Calling Flush on the ETag response writer sends buffered bytes to the client before the response is complete, so the ETag can no longer be set (the request says Flush must not bypass the buffer).

Rules:
- Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no".
- A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no".
- Wording does not matter; the behaviour does.
- For handoffs: count only text that tells the implementor to fix this bug (a reported finding, a fix instruction). Restated acceptance criteria that merely describe the desired behaviour do NOT count as carrying the finding unless the handoff ties them to a reported failure.

=== REVIEW 1 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Declared trailers are lost. Probe `TestProbeTrailerAfterWrite` (httptest.NewServer): handler sets `Trailer: X-Sum`, writes "hello", then sets `X-Sum: abc`. Plain handler gives `trailer=map[X-Sum:[abc]]`; `ETag(h)` gives `trailer=map[X-Sum:[]]` and fails with `PROBE etag: trailer X-Sum = "", want abc`. Cause: `sendHeader` deletes all underlying header keys, including the trailer values set after WriteHeader. The AC7 "snapshot like net/http" wording does not cover trailers, since net/http does send them.
- [minor] Hijack after a buffered write: the buffered bytes are lost, and the status line and headers are not sent. Plain net/http also loses "before" from the body, so this is only partly an ETag regression. ETag additionally logs `response.WriteHeader on hijacked connection` and `response.Write on hijacked connection` from `finish`/`sendHeader`. Probe `TestProbeHijackAfterBufferedWrite`.
- [minor] `If-None-Match: *` with a second header line: the probe I wrote also matched `"x"`, so it did not test the `*` rule. Not reproduced as a bug.
- [minor] `Content-Encoding` is absent on a 304 from `Compress(ETag(h))`, and `Compress(ETag(h))` gives gzip and identity the same ETag. This is the misordering the doc comment warns about, not a code defect.
- [minor] `FEATURE_FLOW.md` is an untracked file in the workspace that the handoff does not mention. Check whether it belongs in the change.
=== REVIEW 2 FINDINGS ===
- [minor] Earlier blocking finding (declared trailers set after body lost): now passes. See CHECKS.
- [minor] Earlier minor finding (finish writes to a hijacked connection): finish returns early on `ew.hijacked`. Not reproduced with a live hijack; verified by reading and by TestETagHijackThenReturn.
- [minor] FEATURE_FLOW.md is an untracked file at the repo root and is not part of the change. Remove it or confirm it is an orchestrator artifact.
- [minor] HEAD with an empty body, no ETag, and `If-None-Match: *` gets 304 with no ETag. RFC-consistent, but it sits awkwardly with AC4's "no ETag for empty HEAD". Reproduced; decide whether it is intended.
- [minor] `WriteHeader(50)` panics in finish with "invalid WriteHeader code 50". A plain handler panics the same way, so this is parity, not a regression.
=== IMPLEMENTOR HANDOFF 1 (sent after review 1) ===
GOAL: Fix two reproduced bugs in the new ETag middleware (repo /tmp/ff-eval-p7kq4yif/workspace, files middleware/etag.go and middleware/etag_test.go), test first.
FILES: middleware/etag.go (etagResponseWriter: sendHeader wipes the underlying header map and replaces it with the snapshot; finish writes after the handler returns), middleware/etag_test.go.
CONSTRAINTS: Only touch those two files. Keep the existing behaviour and tests otherwise. Standard library only. Keep the fix small.
Bugs:
1. [blocking] Trailers are lost. With httptest.NewServer: handler sets `w.Header().Set("Trailer", "X-Sum")`, writes "hello", then sets `w.Header().Set("X-Sum", "abc")`. Without ETag, the client's resp.Trailer["X-Sum"] is "abc"; with ETag it's empty, because sendHeader deletes the late-set value. Trailers set with the `http.TrailerPrefix` ("Trailer:X-Foo") form after the write must survive too. Fix: before sendHeader replaces the headers, keep the handler's live values for the declared trailer names (from the snapshot's "Trailer" header values, comma-separated) and for any http.TrailerPrefix keys, and put them back into the underlying header map after the body is written (both in finish and in the Flush/stream path; streaming writes already go straight to the live map, so check that path just works). Also do this on the 200 path and the non-200 pass-through path. On a 304 there is no body, so trailers don't matter there.
2. [minor] After the handler hijacks the connection via Hijack(), finish still calls WriteHeader/Write on the hijacked response (net/http logs "response.WriteHeader on hijacked connection"). Record a successful Hijack and make finish do nothing after it.
Tests: add a real-server trailer test (both declared-Trailer and TrailerPrefix forms) and a hijack-then-return test that asserts finish doesn't write (e.g. use a fake hijackable ResponseWriter that records WriteHeader/Write calls after Hijack).
ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- AC1 Signature & placement: `func ETag(next http.Handler) http.Handler` in `middleware/etag.go` with a doc comment that says it buffers whole GET/HEAD responses in memory, how If-None-Match is matched, and that it should be registered outside (before) Compress so each encoding gets its own ETag. Tests in `middleware/etag_test.go` (package middleware, httptest.NewRecorder / t.Run table style). No new package-level identifier may collide with existing ones (`etagHeaders` already exists in nocache.go).
- AC2 Strong ETag: for GET with a final status of 200 (explicit WriteHeader(200), implicit via Write, or writing nothing) and no `ETag` header set by the handler, the response carries `ETag: "<hex>"` (strong, double-quoted, no `W/`) computed from the exact body bytes (e.g. SHA-256 hex, may be truncated to >=16 bytes); same body -> same ETag, different body -> different ETag; body and other headers reach the client unchanged.
  Hostile: empty body on GET (ETag still set, consistently); a body written in many small Writes gets the same ETag as the same body written once; a 1 MiB body.
- AC3 A handler-set ETag (strong or weak, e.g. `W/"v1"`) is kept verbatim, never overwritten, and is used for If-None-Match matching.
- AC4 HEAD is buffered the same way. If the HEAD handler wrote body bytes, the ETag is computed from them (equal to GET's for the same bytes). If a HEAD handler wrote zero bytes and set no ETag, do NOT set an ETag (an empty-body hash would be wrong). A handler-set ETag on HEAD is still honored for 304.
- AC5 304: when the request's If-None-Match matches the response's ETag (generated or handler-set) and the final status would be 200, respond 304 with no body. Keep ETag, Cache-Control, Content-Location, Date, Expires, Vary and other headers, but remove Content-Type, Content-Length and Content-Encoding (like net/http's ServeContent writeNotModified). Applies to GET and HEAD.
- AC6 Matching per RFC 9110 §8.8.3.2 / §13.1.2: weak comparison (`W/"x"` matches `"x"` and vice versa; opaque-tags compared byte-for-byte, case-sensitive); comma-separated lists with optional whitespace around members; multiple If-None-Match header lines are combined; `*` (alone) matches any 200 GET/HEAD response.
  Hostile: `"a,b"` (comma inside quotes is legal) must match ETag `"a,b"` and must NOT match ETag `"a"` or `"b"`; unquoted tokens (`abc`), unterminated quotes (`"abc`), `W/abc`, lowercase `w/"x"`, empty header value, `,,` and stray whitespace never match and never panic; `"x"` must not match `"xy"` (no prefix/substring matching); empty members before a valid one (`, ,"x"`) still match `"x"`; a malformed handler-set ETag (e.g. unquoted `abc`) never matches anything except `*`.
- AC7 Pass-through: methods other than GET/HEAD (POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS...) are not wrapped at all: the handler gets the original ResponseWriter, no ETag added, If-None-Match ignored. GET/HEAD responses with any status other than 200 (201, 204, 206, 301, 304, 404, 500...) are written through unchanged: same status, headers and body, no ETag added, no 304 conversion even if If-None-Match matches a handler-set ETag.
  Hostile: handler calls WriteHeader twice (first wins, like net/http); 1xx informational WriteHeader (e.g. 103 Early Hints) is forwarded immediately and is not treated as the final status; a 206 from http.ServeContent passes through; headers the handler sets after WriteHeader/first Write do not reach the client (match net/http: snapshot headers at that point).
- AC8 Wrapped-writer capabilities (sibling: middleware/compress.go compressResponseWriter): Flush (direct or via http.ResponseController) must actually stream: buffering stops, buffered status/headers/body are written unchanged without an ETag, later writes go straight through, and the underlying Flush is called; Hijack and Push are forwarded to the underlying writer with `chi/middleware: ...` errors when unavailable; `Unwrap() http.ResponseWriter` is provided. Errors from the underlying Write are returned to the caller.
- AC9 README: a `| [ETag] | ... |` row in the "Core middlewares" table between [Compress] and [ContentCharset], padded like its neighbours, and `[ETag]: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware#ETag` in the link list between the same neighbours.
- AC10 `gofmt -l .` prints nothing, `go vet ./...` and `go test -race ./...` pass; standard library only.
- AC11 Trailers: trailer values the handler sets after writing the body (declared via the `Trailer` header, or keyed with http.TrailerPrefix) reach the client exactly as without the middleware. After a successful Hijack, the middleware writes nothing more.
CHECKS: while working: `go test -race -run 'ETag' ./middleware`. At the end: `gofmt -l .` (empty), `go vet ./...`, `go test -race ./...`.
